title: fix: allow Mouse Without Borders pairing across valid Microsoft signer certificates

review.body_prefix:
### Qualified current-revision assessment

The signer comparison no longer requires the two Microsoft-signed peers to have identical leaf-certificate bytes. Each peer must independently satisfy the existing trusted-Microsoft-signature policy; the surrounding process-identity gates remain in place. This addresses legitimate signer rotation without treating arbitrary signed binaries as acceptable peers.

The exact affected project builds with analyzers enabled, and all 50 selected Mouse Without Borders IPC security tests pass. The distinct-signer fixture executed successfully. Candidate discovery already tries curated Windows/dependency paths first and returns on the first suitable peer; full DLL enumeration is a fallback. The exception variable is used by its type filter, so the proposed removal would be invalid.

No additional required correction is established in that scope. This does not assert a fresh zero-finding approval, completed pairing/runtime validation, or that the open covering fix is shipped or resolves every cause of the reported pairing failures.

The current complete caller trace confirms expected executable name, equal/nested directory, held process instance, intended user and session checks precede independent trusted signatures. The distinct-signer fixture already uses curated candidates before lazy directory fallback and short-circuits on success. The retained exact build and50 IPC tests pass; no failing supported fixture image or complete-gate bypass is established.
